questions.question:
Let p,q, r, s represent the following propositions.

p: x[latex]\in[/latex]{8,9,10,11,12}
q: x is a composite number
r: x is a perfect square
s: x is a prime number

The integer x[latex]\geq[/latex]2 which satisfies [latex]\neg((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge (\neg r \vee \neg s))[/latex] is ________.
questions.explanation:
[latex] eg((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge( eg r\vee eg s))\equiv(p\wedge eg q)\vee(r\wedge s)[/latex]

- [latex]r\wedge s[/latex] (perfect square and prime) is impossible.
- So we need [latex]p\wedge eg q[/latex]: x in {8, 9, 10, 11, 12} and not composite. Only 11 qualifies.

Answer: 11

questions.question: A queue is implemented using an array such that ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations are performed efficiently. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT (n refers to the number of items in the queue)?

options.B:
At most one operation can be performed in O(1) time but the worst case time for

options.C: The worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
options.D: Worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](logn)

questions.question:
A function [latex]f:\mathbb{N}^{+}\rightarrow \mathbb{N}^{+}[/latex], defined on the set of positive integers [latex]\mathbb{N}^{+}[/latex], satisfies the following properties:
f(n)=f(n/2) if n is even
f(n)=f(n+5) if n is odd
Let R={[latex]i|\exists j:f(j)=i[/latex]} be the set of distinct values that f takes. The maximum possible size of R is ____.
questions.explanation:

- If n is a multiple of 5, n/2 (when even) and n + 5 are still multiples of 5.
- If n is not a multiple of 5, neither are n/2 and n + 5.

Inside: + first, 5 + 1 = 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]-[/latex] 6 [latex]-[/latex] 7. [latex]-[/latex] is right associative: [latex]2-(6-7)=2-(-1)=3[/latex].

[latex]3*3=9[/latex]

Answer: 9

questions.question:
Consider the following proposed solution for the critical section problem. There are n processes: [latex]P_{0}...P_{n-1}[/latex] . In the code,function [latex]pmax[/latex] returns an integer not smaller than any of its arguments. For all i, t[i] is initialized to zero.

Which one of the following is TRUE about the above solution?

options.A: At most one process can be in the critical section at any time
options.B: The bounded wait condition is satisfied

questions.explanation:
This is a bakery-style algorithm: a process enters only after every other process with a smaller (non-zero) ticket has finished, so mutual exclusion holds.

But two processes can pick the same ticket (pmax is not atomic). Then each waits for the other (t[j] [latex]\le[/latex] t[i] holds both ways) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock, so progress and bounded waiting also fail.

Answer: At most one process can be in the critical section at any time

questions.question: In a process, the number of cycles to failure decreases exponentially with an increase in load. At a load of 80 units, it takes 100 cycles for failure. Let cycles [latex]N=Ae^{-kL}[/latex]. Halving the load from 80 to 40 multiplies N by 100, so [latex]e^{40k}=100[/latex].

From L = 40 (10000 cycles) to 5000 cycles: [latex]e^{k(L-40)}=2\Rightarrow L-40=\frac{40\ln2}{\ln100}=40\times\frac{0.301}{2}=6.02[/latex]

L = 46.02

Answer: 46.02
